measures.title: Authorizing the City's Salary Commission to Set the Mayor's Salary
measures.summary: A proposed amendment to the Bellingham City Charter. The Charter now says the Mayor's salary may at no time be less than that of the highest-paid City official or employee. The amendment would delete that requirement and have the City's independent salary commission, which already sets City Council salaries, set the Mayor's salary.
measures.yesMeans: The City's salary commission would set the Mayor's salary, and the Mayor's pay would no longer be tied to the highest-paid City employee.
measures.noMeans: The Charter would keep requiring that the Mayor's salary be no less than that of the highest-paid City official or employee.

measures.title: Streamlining the City's Contract Review Process to Allow Electronic Signatures
measures.summary: A proposed amendment to the Bellingham City Charter. The Charter now requires the Mayor to sign all city contracts, bonds and instruments, and the finance director to attest the Mayor's signature and affix the City seal. The amendment would remove those requirements, let the Mayor's designee sign contracts, and allow electronic signatures.
measures.yesMeans: The Mayor's designee could sign city contracts, and the City could use electronic signatures without the attestation and seal requirements.
measures.noMeans: The Charter would keep requiring the Mayor's signature, the finance director's attestation and the City seal on city contracts.

measures.title: Prohibition of Algorithmic Price-Fixing in the Rental Market
measures.summary: A citizen initiative that would add a chapter to the Bellingham Municipal Code. It would prohibit landlords from agreeing with each other to set rental prices and prohibit paid algorithmic coordinating services that use rental market data to recommend rents, lease renewal terms or occupancy levels to multiple landlords. It would create a private right of action, whistleblower and anti-retaliation protections for tenants and employees, and civil and criminal penalties; it would not apply to hotels, motels or short-term rentals.
measures.yesMeans: Bellingham would prohibit rental price-fixing agreements and algorithmic rent-coordinating services, with the listed remedies and penalties.
measures.noMeans: Bellingham would not adopt this chapter prohibiting algorithmic rent-setting services.

measures.title: Levy Lid Lift for Public Safety and Essential Community Services
measures.summary: Under Resolution No. 26-1148, the City of Lynden asks to raise its regular property tax levy above the usual limit to fund police and fire, park and street maintenance, restoring eliminated staff positions, reopening City Hall on Fridays, and offsetting lost funding for the Lynden Community/Senior Center. It would set a maximum 2026 levy, collected in 2027, of $1.54304 per $1,000 of assessed value, allow 3% annual increases for 2027-2035, and use the 2035 levy to calculate future levy limits.
measures.yesMeans: Lynden could levy up to $1.54304 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection, with 3% annual increases through 2035, for the listed services.
measures.noMeans: Lynden's regular property tax levy would stay under the existing limit.
